subject: SLO impact sizing & warm-pool tradeoffs
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@olivepay.com>, Jamie Cross <jamie.cross@olivepay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: performance targets & autoscale follow-ups

Hi Alex / Jamie —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the concrete next steps we discussed so your engineering team can validate SLO fit. I attached an initial sizing matrix (slo-impact-matrix.xlsx) and our runbook stub for burst behavior (scale-runbook-v1.pdf).

Recap / confirmed targets you gave us:
- P95 generation latency target: <= 75ms (end-to-end, app -> Redwood -> token stream)
- Sustained concurrent sessions: ~600 per region (US-east primary)
- Peak concurrent windows: up to 2,000 active sessions for short bursts (under 5 minutes)
- Streaming requirement: partial token delivery during prompt streaming + early stop support
- Expected burst QPS: up to 5,000 requests over 1–3 minute ramps during marketing spikes

Open questions we promised to follow up on:
1) Warm-pool sizing and expected scale-up times across the path from cold -> prewarmed -> live instances.
2) How queueing fallback will affect tail latency for streaming responses.
3) Cost tradeoffs for leaving warm instances idle vs. faster recovery from cold starts.

Suggested next steps (action items):
- We’ll run a brief A/B simulation with two warm-pool configurations (200 vs 600 pre-warmed instances) and share latency/throughput and cost delta. Marcus / Aditya to scope the sim.
- Demo: stream-focused walkthrough where we hit partial-token delivery and observe queueing behavior. Can you confirm a 60 minute slot this week (we suggested Wed 11:00–12:00 PT)?
- OlivePay: confirm whether you need strict SLA guarantees for peak windows or if best-effort with fallback is acceptable for an initial onboarding.

Attachments: slo-impact-matrix.xlsx (first pass), scale-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook outline)

Thanks — I’ll loop in Marcus & Aditya to schedule the sim and cost-run.

—
Laura Bennett

Hi Laura —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifying questions before we commit to a demo and the A/B sim:

1) Billing model question: how are warm pre-warmed instances billed on Redwood? Is there an hourly charge once pre-warmed, or only on execution? We need to map to our finance team's capacity-cost expectations.
2) Queueing fallback: if we move requests into the overflow queue during a ramp, what's a realistic additional latency for the first streamed tokens? We’re worried about visible lag to end-users during checkout flows.
3) A/B scenario: can you include a mid-point option (e.g., 350 warm instances) in the sim? Our spikes are usually shorter than 2 minutes but happen frequently — we want to understand diminishing returns.

Proposed demo slot: Wed 11:00 PT works for me. Jamie will likely join pinging in a separate calendar invite.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Turner

Alex — thanks, great questions. Quick answers and what we’ll include in the A/B sim and demo: 

Billing & pre-warm economics
- Two main pricing levers: reserved/dedicated capacity (committed monthly) vs. pre-warmed instances attached to your burst band.
- Pre-warmed instances incur a modest standby charge when idle (roughly ~12–20% of an active GPU-hour depending on hardware class) because they reserve memory and kernel contexts. We’ll produce a cost delta table that shows 200 / 350 / 600 pre-warm examples.

Queueing fallback and streaming latency
- Overflow queue is designed to maintain throughput while keeping SLOs for new requests; however, streaming first-token latency will see additional wait equal to the time to pop from queue and allocate a slot (typically 10–40ms under target load; could be higher under extreme saturation).
- For streaming, early token delivery can be preserved by prioritizing prefix-cache hits and routing long-running sessions to warm instances. We’ll instrument the sim to surface first-byte and p50/p95 stream token latencies.

A/B sim plan (what Marcus / Aditya will run)
- Profiles: 200 pre-warm, 350 pre-warm, 600 pre-warm (sustained baseline is 600 concurrent sessions).
- Ramp shape: 0 -> peak (5,000 QPS) over 90s, hold 120s, ramp down 60s.
- Metrics: p50/p95 end-to-end latency, first-stream-token latency, error rate, CPU/GPU utilization, and cost per 1M tokens.
- Deliverable: spreadsheet with latency curves and cost delta for each configuration (we’ll attach sle-impact-matrix-v2.xlsx).

Demo: Wed 11:00 PT confirmed from our side. We’ll focus on streaming behavior + the queueing fallback demonstration using a short synthetic load and a small canary against a pre-warmed pool. I’ll send a calendar invite with dial-in and demo agenda.

Attachments: I’m attaching an updated sizing worksheet (slo-impact-matrix-v2.xlsx) that includes the 350 mid-point and the cost delta columns.

Let me know if you want us to include a separate run showing the impact of a cache layer (prefix KV cache) vs no-cache — that typically reduces need for large warm pools for repeat traffic.

—
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
